item.content:encoded: As far as I know, nothing particularly unpleasant happened in Patagonia that year, though Lord Blackwood might tell us otherwise at some point. Blackwood temporarily dying in 1893 is a reference to that being the year when Arthur Conan Doyle killed off Sherlock Holmes, only to resurrect him by public demand a few years later.

item.content:encoded:
Also, could these Blackwood related tales be tagged with "blackwood", or would that be violating the site's tagging policy?

I'm pretty certain that creating a 'blackwood' tag would be just fine. After all, that's how almost all tags came into existence - by authors deciding to create them. And this tag would have an obvious use. And I've done exactly the same thing (before being staff, too). I say go for it. If you're really worried, TroyL and Raven Mackenzie would be the people to ask about that specifically; Troy because he's the admin primarily overseeing tags (unless that's changed in the last couple months or so), and Mackenzie because she is the person most involved in handling tags.

This is the first Blackwood article I've read, and it's absolutely excellent. I loved the 'slug' bit in particular, but the thing that shines here is the style and the well-written dialogue.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's in keeping with how he's addressed in the original article's interview log. That article doesn't even name him SCP-662-1 at all, probably because it's an older one and that usage hadn't been standardized yet at the time. I created that designation for this tale because just calling him Mr. Deeds in the intro felt inappropriate, but it works in the log himself since we want Deeds to cooperate and calling him that seems to make him comfortable.

(If we want to really get picky, convention would dictate that a valet be addressed simply by his last name without the courtesy title, so he should be "Deeds" and not "Mr. Deeds", but i'm not going to go rewriting someone else's SCP for the purposes of my tale.)
